::: {.key-question}
What is the average educational attainment for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in the NEPHU catchment?
:::

## Highest Level of School Completed

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# High school completion - entire population, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
school_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Education_School_LGA.csv",
                                variable = "school_year") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!school_year %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable")) 

# Data wrangling
school_lga <- school_lga %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(school_year = dplyr::case_when(
    school_year == "Year 12 or equivalent" ~ "Year 12",
    school_year == "Year 11 or equivalent" ~ "Year 9-11",
    school_year == "Year 10 or equivalent" ~ "Year 9-11",
    school_year == "Year 9 or equivalent"  ~ "Year 9-11",
    school_year == "Year 8 or below"       ~ "Year 8 and below",
    school_year == "Did not go to school"  ~ "Year 8 and below",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = school_year,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(year_12_prop   = aboriginal_n_year_12 / aboriginal_total * 100,
                year_9_11_prop = aboriginal_n_year_9_11 / aboriginal_total * 100,
                year_8_prop    = aboriginal_n_year_8_and_below / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                year_12_n = aboriginal_n_year_12,
                year_12_prop,
                year_9_11_n = aboriginal_n_year_9_11,
                year_9_11_prop,
                year_8_n = aboriginal_n_year_8_and_below,
                year_8_prop,
                aboriginal_total)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# High school completion - entire population, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
school_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Education_School_AgeSex.csv",
                                      variable = "school_year") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!school_year %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling - by age and sex
school_agesex <- school_agesex %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(school_year = dplyr::case_when(
    school_year == "Year 12 or equivalent" ~ "Year 12",
    school_year == "Year 11 or equivalent" ~ "Year 9-11",
    school_year == "Year 10 or equivalent" ~ "Year 9-11",
    school_year == "Year 9 or equivalent"  ~ "Year 9-11",
    school_year == "Year 8 or below"       ~ "Year 8 and below",
    school_year == "Did not go to school"  ~ "Year 8 and below",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = school_year,
                          dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_total = aboriginal_n_year_12 + aboriginal_n_year_9_11 + aboriginal_n_year_8_and_below,
                year_12_prop     = aboriginal_n_year_12 / aboriginal_total * 100,
                year_9_11_prop   = aboriginal_n_year_9_11 / aboriginal_total * 100,
                year_8_prop      = aboriginal_n_year_8_and_below / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.na(.), 0)),
                across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.nan(.), 0))) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(age_group,
                sex,
                year_12_n = aboriginal_n_year_12,
                year_12_prop,
                year_9_11_n = aboriginal_n_year_9_11,
                year_9_11_prop,
                year_8_n = aboriginal_n_year_8_and_below,
                year_8_prop,
                aboriginal_total)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 48% (n = 4,020) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census had completed Year 12 or equivalent, and a further 45% (n = 3,739) had completed Years 9-11 or equivalent. 

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who had completed Year 12 or equivalent ranged from 606 (Whittlesea LGA) to 118 (Manningham LGA). 

- The percentage of people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who had completed Year 12 or equivalent ranged from 69% (Boroondara LGA) to 41% (Yarra Ranges LGA). 

- Younger people were more likely to have a Year 12 or equivalent education, and females were more likely to have a Year 12 or equivalent education than males across all age groups.

## Year 12 Completion

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 5](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/student-learning-potential/): Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students achieve their full learning potential**

Target: By 2031, increase the proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people (aged 20-24 years) attaining Year 12 or equivalent qualification to 96%.
:::

::: {style="height: 1em;"}
:::

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Year 12 completion - trend over time
# Data from ABS Census via CtG Information Repository
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in ABS data
year12_trend <- f_read_ctg_indigenous("CTG05_Learning_Potential_Data_Tables.xlsx",
                                      data_sheet     = "Table CtG5A.1",
                                      column_select  = c(indigenous_status = "x3",
                                                         year = "x4",
                                                         "vic",
                                                         "unit"),
                                      fill_variables = vars(indigenous_status, year),
                                      row_select     = 1:20)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Year 12 completion - young adults
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data wrangling
year12_youth <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Education_School_YoungAdult.csv",
                                     variable = "school_year") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!school_year %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(school_year = dplyr::case_when(
    school_year == "Year 12 or equivalent" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no"))

# Data wrangling - by LGA
year12_lga <- year12_youth %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = school_year,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# Data wrangling - by sex
year12_sex <- year12_youth %>%
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = school_year,
                          dichot   = "yes") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(age_group == "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::bind_rows(year12_lga %>% 
                     dplyr::filter(lga_name == "NEPHU") %>% 
                     #
                     dplyr::mutate(age_group = "NEPHU",
                                   sex       = "NEPHU") %>% 
                     #
                     dplyr::select(-lga_name))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/), compiled from the ABS Census for the Census years between 2001 and 2021, as well as the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- The percentage of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 20-24 years living in Victoria with a Year 12 or equivalent education increased from 49% in 2001 to 73% in 2021. 

- Overall, 74% (n = 853) of people aged 20-24 years living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census had a Year 12 or equivalent education. This was lower than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (89%). 

- The number of people aged 20-24 years living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who had a Year 12 or equivalent education ranged from 141 (Whittlesea LGA) to 21 (Manningham LGA). 

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 20-24 years with a Year 12 or equivalent education and the number expected if the rate was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Hume and Knox LGAs. 

- The percentage of people aged 20-24 years living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who had a Year 12 or equivalent education ranged from 90% (Yarra LGA) to 65% (Knox LGA). 

- All 12 NEPHU LGAs were below the Closing the Gap target of 96% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 20-24 years attaining Year 12 or an equivalent qualification. 

- 79% (n = 436) of females living in the NEPHU catchment aged 20-24 years who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census had a Year 12 or equivalent education, compared to 71% (n = 417) of males.

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- In recent years there has been significant growth in the number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander students graduating Year 12. 

- Consultation feedback during the development of this report stressed the importance of [different pathways](https://www.vic.gov.au/study-options-year-11-and-12) by which qualifications can be attained (e.g. VCAL), including accommodation for different learning styles. 

- The [Victorian Aboriginal Education Association Incorporated (VAEAI)](https://www.vic.gov.au/victorian-aboriginal-education-association-inc-vaeai) and [Victorian Aboriginal Community Services Association (VASCAL)](https://www.vacsal.org.au/) were credited with significant achievements in this area by stakeholders during the development of this report. VAEAI is the peak Koorie community organization for education and training in Victoria, advising education and government on ways to improve educational outcomes for students. VASCAL also provides advice to government and is a major provider of services to the Aboriginal community including an Aboriginal Early School Leavers and Youth Employment Program.

## Highest Level of Education

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Highest level of education - entire population, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
qualification <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Education_Qualification_LGA.csv",
                                   variable = "qualification") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!qualification %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable", "Supplementary Codes")) 

# Data wrangling
qualification_lga <- qualification %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(qualification = dplyr::case_when(
    qualification == "Postgraduate Degree Level"                       ~ "Postgraduate",
    qualification == "Graduate Diploma and Graduate Certificate Level" ~ "Postgraduate",
    qualification == "Bachelor Degree Level"                           ~ "Undergraduate",
    qualification == "Advanced Diploma and Diploma Level"              ~ "Certificate and Diploma",
    qualification == "Certificate III & IV Level"                      ~ "Certificate and Diploma",
    qualification == "Certificate I & II Level"                        ~ "High School",
    qualification == "Secondary Education - Years 10 and above"        ~ "High School",
    qualification == "Secondary Education - Years 9 and below"         ~ "High School",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = qualification,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(postgrad_prop        = aboriginal_n_postgraduate / aboriginal_total * 100,
                undergrad_prop       = aboriginal_n_undergraduate / aboriginal_total * 100,
                certificate_prop     = aboriginal_n_certificate_and_diploma / aboriginal_total * 100,
                year_highschool_prop = aboriginal_n_high_school / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                postgrad_n = aboriginal_n_postgraduate,
                postgrad_prop,
                undergrad_n = aboriginal_n_undergraduate,
                undergrad_prop,
                certificate_n = aboriginal_n_certificate_and_diploma,
                certificate_prop,
                year_highschool_n = aboriginal_n_high_school,
                year_highschool_prop,
                aboriginal_total)

qualification_lga_tertiary <- qualification_lga %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(tertiary_n    = postgrad_n + undergrad_n + certificate_n,
                tertiary_prop = tertiary_n / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                tertiary_n,
                tertiary_prop)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Highest level of education - entire population, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
qualification_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Education_Qualification_AgeSex.csv",
                                             variable = "qualification") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!qualification %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable", "Supplementary Codes")) 

# Data wrangling
qualification_agesex <- qualification_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(qualification = dplyr::case_when(
    qualification == "Postgraduate Degree Level"                       ~ "Postgraduate",
    qualification == "Graduate Diploma and Graduate Certificate Level" ~ "Postgraduate",
    qualification == "Bachelor Degree Level"                           ~ "Undergraduate",
    qualification == "Advanced Diploma and Diploma Level"              ~ "Certificate and Diploma",
    qualification == "Certificate III & IV Level"                      ~ "Certificate and Diploma",
    qualification == "Certificate I & II Level"                        ~ "High School",
    qualification == "Secondary Education - Years 10 and above"        ~ "High School",
    qualification == "Secondary Education - Years 9 and below"         ~ "High School",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = qualification,
                          dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_total     = aboriginal_n_postgraduate + aboriginal_n_undergraduate + aboriginal_n_certificate_and_diploma + aboriginal_n_high_school,
                postgrad_prop        = aboriginal_n_postgraduate / aboriginal_total * 100,
                undergrad_prop       = aboriginal_n_undergraduate / aboriginal_total * 100,
                certificate_prop     = aboriginal_n_certificate_and_diploma / aboriginal_total * 100,
                year_highschool_prop = aboriginal_n_high_school / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.na(.), 0)),
                across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.nan(.), 0))) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(age_group,
                sex,
                postgrad_n = aboriginal_n_postgraduate,
                postgrad_prop,
                undergrad_n = aboriginal_n_undergraduate,
                undergrad_prop,
                certificate_n = aboriginal_n_certificate_and_diploma,
                certificate_prop,
                year_highschool_n = aboriginal_n_high_school,
                year_highschool_prop,
                aboriginal_total)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 49% (n = 3,828) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census had a tertiary qualification (Certificate III or above). This was lower than for non-Indigenous people living in the [NEPHU catchment](https://nephu.org.au/reports-and-publications/nephu-population-profile-general-report-2025/) (55%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who had a tertiary qualification (Certificate III or above) ranged from 598 (Whittlesea LGA) to 87 (Manningham LGA). 

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who had a tertiary qualification (Certificate III or above) ranged from 61% (Yarra LGA) to 41% (Hume LGA). 

- Younger people were more likely to have a tertiary qualification than older people. 

- Females were more likely to have a university degree (undergraduate and/or postgraduate) than males.

## Tertiary Qualifications

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 6](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/further-education-pathways/): Students reach their full potential through further education pathways**

Target: By 2031, increase the proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people aged 25–34 years who have completed a tertiary qualification (Certificate III and above) to 70%.
:::

::: {style="height: 1em;"}
:::

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tertiary qualifications - trend over time
# Data from ABS Census via CtG Information Repository
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in ABS data
uni_trend <- f_read_ctg_indigenous("CTG06_Education_Pathways_Data_Tables.xlsx",
                                   data_sheet     = "Table CtG6A.1",
                                   column_select  = c(indigenous_status = "x3",
                                                      year = "x4",
                                                      "vic",
                                                      "unit"),
                                   fill_variables = vars(indigenous_status, year),
                                   row_select     = 1:20)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tertiary qualifications - young adults
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data wrangling
uni_youth <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Education_Qualification_YoungAdult.csv",
                                  variable = "qualification") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!qualification %in% c("Not stated", "Not applicable", "Supplementary Codes")) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(qualification = dplyr::case_when(
    qualification == "Postgraduate Degree Level"                       ~ "yes",
    qualification == "Graduate Diploma and Graduate Certificate Level" ~ "yes",
    qualification == "Bachelor Degree Level"                           ~ "yes",
    qualification == "Advanced Diploma and Diploma Level"              ~ "yes",
    qualification == "Certificate III & IV Level"                      ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no"))

# Data wrangling - by LGA
uni_lga <- uni_youth %>% 
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = qualification,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# Data wrangling - by sex
uni_sex <- uni_youth %>%
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = qualification,
                          dichot   = "yes") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(age_group == "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::bind_rows(uni_lga %>% 
                     dplyr::filter(lga_name == "NEPHU") %>%
                     #
                     dplyr::mutate(age_group = "NEPHU",
                                   sex       = "NEPHU") %>% 
                     #
                     dplyr::select(-lga_name))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/), compiled from the ABS Census for the Census years between 2001 and 2021, as well as the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census). 

- The percentage of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 25-34 years living in Victoria with a tertiary qualification (Certificate III and above) increased from 29% in 2001 to 59% in 2021. 

- Overall, 65% (n = 1,155) of people aged 25-34 years living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census had a tertiary qualification (Certificate III and above). This was lower than for non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (81%). 

- The number of people aged 25-34 years living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who had a tertiary qualification (Certificate III and above) ranged from 186 (Darebin LGA) to 15 (Manningham LGA). 

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people aged 25-34 years who had a tertiary qualification (Certificate III and above) and the expected number if the proportion was the same as for non-Indigenous people was biggest for Darebin LGA and Hume LGAs. 

- The percentage of people aged 25-34 years living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who had a tertiary qualification (Certificate III and above) ranged from 91% (Nillumbik LGA) to 56% (Knox LGA). 

- 71% (n = 632) of females living in the NEPHU catchment aged 25-34 years who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census had a tertiary qualification, compared to 59% (n = 523) of males.

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- 4 out of 12 LGAs in the NEPHU catchment currently above the Closing the Gap target, showing the progress that has been made in achieving this target.  

- Multiple Aboriginal Community-Controlled Organisations in Victoria are now offering programs for tertiary education.

- For example, the [Victorian Aboriginal Community Services Association (VASCAL)](https://www.vacsal.org.au/), offers a Certificate IV and Diploma of Community Services. The [Victorian Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation (VACCHO)](https://www.vaccho.org.au/) also offers a range of Diplomas, including a Diploma of Counselling and a Diploma of Business.
